newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were hardly changed in late trading on Thursday despite higher Malaysian values as sentiment remained weak, traders said.
They said olein was quoted at 1,350-55 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, but offers were also heard at 1,340-45 rupiah. Crude palm oil was holding at around 1,145 rupiah in Medan.
"Gains in the Malaysian market had no impact here," one trader said. "(Local) buyers got afraid when some offers came in at 1,340 rupiah. There's still some downside left."
Traders said supply remained ample and fresh shipments were heading for Jakarta.

They said talk that a senior executive from a plantation house had told his customers in Semarang that olein prices could gradually ease to 1,300 rupiah seem to suggest the possibility of market operations by state logistics agency BULOG.
But the traders said government action, if any, to reduce the price of olein would only come ahead of the Moslem Ramadan fasting month early next year.
"The executive's remarks are giving rise to much speculation over the price direction of olein since he (executive) has good links with the government," one trader said.
Traders are speculating that if olein prices breach the 1,325-rupiah support level, they would head towards 1,300.
They also said a 5,500-tonne shipment of palm olein imported by BULOG from Malaysia had arrived in Jakarta, but it was not immediately clear if the consignment had been pre-sold.

Data from Belawan Port showed that 4,500 tonnes of olein was scheduled to leave the North Sumatran port on Thursday for Pasir Gudang, Malaysia. The MT Bobo left the port for Jakarta with 4,000 tonnes of olein on Sunday, a day after the MT Bumagh left for Jakarta with 4,200 tonnes of olein.
